title: Point-slope and standard form
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings, word problems, and an 'is this right?' item. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation behind the item ('ps M X Y': the line y − Y = M(x − X) written as y = mx + b; 'std A B C slope|xint|yint|intercepts|line': the slope, x-intercept, y-intercept, both intercepts, or y = mx + b form of the line Ax + By = C), used only by the test that checks the answer key.
directions: Show your work. Write equations in the form y = mx + b. Write fractions in simplest form.

items.prompt: Write y + 3 = 4(x − 2) in the form y = mx + b.
Water is pumped into a tank at 3 gallons per minute. After 4 minutes the tank holds 20 gallons. Write an equation for the gallons y in the tank after x minutes, in the form y = mx + b.
items.answer: y = 3x + 8 (y − 20 = 3(x − 4); the tank started with 8 gallons)

items.prompt: Find the x-intercept and the y-intercept of the line 3x + 4y = 24.
Rewrite 6x − 2y = 8 in the form y = mx + b.
items.answer: y = 3x − 4 (−2y = −6x + 8, then divide every term by −2)

items.prompt: At a school fair, adult tickets cost $5 and student tickets cost $2. The fair took in $60, so 5x + 2y = 60, where x is the number of adult tickets and y the number of student tickets. If no adult tickets were sold, how many student tickets were sold?
Priya rewrites 2x + 5y = 10 in slope-intercept form and gets y = −2x + 10. Is she right? Explain, and write the correct equation.
items.answer: y = −(2/5)x + 2 (No: after 5y = −2x + 10 she must divide every term by 5)

items.prompt: Write y − 6 = −3(x + 1) in the form y = mx + b.
A line has a slope of 1/2 and passes through the point (4, −1). Write its equation in the form y = mx + b.
What is the slope of the line 5x − 2y = 10?
Rewrite 8x + 4y = 12 in the form y = mx + b.

A club orders sandwiches at $4 each and salads at $3 each, and spends exactly $48: 4x + 3y = 48, where x is the number of sandwiches and y the number of salads. If they order only sandwiches, how many do they get?
Devon wants the line with slope 5 through the point (2, 3). He writes y − 2 = 5(x − 3), which gives y = 5x − 13. Is he right? Explain, and write the correct equation.
items.answer: y = 5x − 7 (No: he swapped x and y; it is y − 3 = 5(x − 2), so y = 5x − 10 + 3)
